question_type: order statistic (85th Hazen percentile, rank lands exactly on the 9th of 10) over one agency column of FFO-3 across ten fiscal years that must be assembled from two or more issues
decisive_step: Which column(s) of TABLE FFO-3 (On-Budget and Off-Budget Outlays by Agency) are 'the Department of Defense': column (5) 'Department of Defense, military' alone, versus (5) plus the separately listed agency column (20) 'Other Defense, civil programs' (and, consistently, (19) 'Corps of Engineers'). Everything else was identical in all four cells: table FFO-3, FY annual rows (est. and to-date rows excluded), latest printing per year, Hazen rank r = 10*0.85+0.5 = 9.0 so the answer is the 9th order statistic with no interpolation. The reference made the column decision in worklog Step 2 ('the DoD series is column (5)') and defended it in Step 6 / solution.json decision 'Which DoD series' (Corps and other defense civil are separate agency columns; the question names one department); its cells are treasury_bulletin_2016_03.txt:676-680 and treasury_bulletin_2021_03.txt:691-695.

It computed the Hazen percentile for the military-only series and for the military+civil sum in one calc (a[26]), then chose the single column on the wording ('Other Defense, civil programs is not a Department', a[25],[27]).

smallest_change.change: Rewrite the last OfficeQA table note so it starts from the entity, not from the sum. Replace 'For a sum over the columns of one row, list the whole row ... and decide for each column whether the question includes it' with: 'An agency, program or item named in the question is the ONE column (or row) whose label names it; do not add neighbouring columns with related words ("Other ...", "... civil programs", "Corps of ...") unless the question says "including", "combined" or lists the parts. Words in the question that repeat the table title or units line ("on-budget and off-budget", "nominal", "in millions") describe the table, not extra columns to add. If you do sum several columns, list the row with show_table --long and name each column you include.'
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a and c already reasoned exactly this way (a[25], c[18]); the escape clause keeps genuine multi-part totals ('including', listed parts) summable. It removes the 'For a sum over the columns' framing, which primes summation.

alternatives.change: Submit-time informational finding (no Accept/Keep offer): when the inputs of the final calc come from two or more columns of the same table row whose labels are different entities (here c5 'Department of Defense, military' and c20 'Other Defense, civil programs', in different table parts), print 'Your sum combines columns (5) and (20), which FFO-3 lists as separate agencies; the question names one entity. Single-column variant (5) = <value>. Submit again to confirm or change.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Pilot-1 analysis showed this is a coin flip across questions (UID0097 was hurt by the opposite direction), competing_candidates was deliberately disabled in b2, and it costs a gate round on every legitimately summed row; it also cannot know which column the question means.

alternatives.change: Three operational fixes that would have cut b's 21 requests toward a's 14 but not changed the column decision: (1) otables: attach an orphan continuation part to its parent when it sits between two parts of the same table, has the same row labels and its column numbers continue the sequence (2020_03 lines 715-737, columns (14)-(24), is parsed as 'TABLE of the' with subtitle 'Department', so --stitch/--cols/--match never reach column (20)); label continuation parts 'part 2', 'part 3' instead of 'part 1 ... continuation'. (2) printings --summary (or default when a shell loop is detected by output size): one line per period and column, e.g. '[FY2011] col (5) Department of Defense, military: latest 2016_09 (treasury_bulletin_2016_09.txt:670) = <value>; 21 printings, unchanged', so a 10-year loop fits one page. (3) When --years excludes every printing of a row, say so: 'row FY2011 is printed in issues 2011_12..2016_09; --years 2020-2025 excludes them' instead of 'check the row label/period and --col'.
alternatives.why_not_first: All four cells saw the correct column (5) values; the wrong cells failed at interpretation, not at reading.

notes: Pattern worth recording for v10: all five text-only runs (a, c, v8 none/prompt/cards) chose the single column; both mechanism-arm runs (b, b2) over-included, even though b2 had a's full advice text. The submit checks cannot see this class of error (an extra column folded into an entity total). The Hazen step was never a differentiator: every cell derived rank 9.0 and no interpolation, and no cell needed external knowledge beyond the (i-0.5)/n formula (rg for 'Hazen' in the corpus finds nothing, a[24], b2[18]). Tool observations: (1) the 2020_03 FFO-3 middle part (columns 14-24) is invisible to stitch/cols/match because the title line was split by a page header ('TABLE of the' / 'Department'), and find_tables reports that issue with two 'part1' entries; (2) printings for a 10-year range x 2 columns is ~50 KB and every cell had to post-process it with sed/tail/rg, so a compact summary mode is the highest-value ergonomic change; (3) --grep is a row filter and three cells used it as a column filter on first contact (a[8], b2[8], c[8]); consider making --grep match column labels too, or printing 'no rows matched; did you mean --match <column>?'; (4) --years means issue years, and its no-match message should state the issues that do print the row.
